On page 8, "Mexican Americans" are singled out as having "special housing requirements." This is not explained and, on the surface, appears inappropriate.
The following typographical errors were observed: page 10, add "acre" following 120; page 11, add "acre" following 35.9.
It is suggested that the item on the removal of wild cherry trees at the Kalamazoo site in the last paragraph on page 18 be reconsidered. The control of tent caterpillars is a basic environmental need for several types of trees and shrubs. The statement that 'spraying of wild cherry trees to prevent tent caterpillars be stopped" should be deleted. The decision to retain the wild cherry trees should be predicated upon their ornamental value relative to other alternative choices of trees.
The proposal to use storm drainage for ground water recharge at the Kalamazoo and Macon sites requires more detail than given on page 19. The Department requests the full text of the method of managing storm drainage as the hazard to pollution of ground water may be greater than the harm created by surface runoff.
Specific questions that bear on the subject are: What is contained in storm drainage? What hydrocarbons are involved? What are the characteristics of soil, geologic strata, and ground water at the two sites?
Sincerely,
T. C. BYERLY
Coordinator, Environmental
Quality Activities
